title: DaVinci Resolve: Level One Edit & Advanced Techniques for Social Video (Mac & PC)
summary: This in-depth tutorial switches between DaVinci Resolve’s UI and hands‑on editing, guiding a beginner from a basic Resolve layout and media import to a complete Level One edit and an outline of an Advanced Edit. It covers importing media (including folder-based import), setting up project settings (timeline resolution and vertical formats for social platforms), fundamental timeline editing (blade tool, trim, and basic inspector adjustments), color grading with LUTs (notably a Sony LUT) and color wheels, audio shaping (normalization and compressor), B‑roll insertion and multi‑track layering, transitions (Push, glitch, and other effects), intro text and logo overlays, masking and tracking for background replacement, cloning/ghosting effects, and the process of exporting with options for captions. The video also demonstrates practical workflow tips for social media content, like vertical timelines, punch-ins, and template-based text—culminating in an advanced edit preview before a final render.

concepts: DaVinci Resolve as a free editor
seven-page layout at the bottom of the UI
plan for the video: Level One basic edit then advanced edit
sections.description: The video opens with a claim that DaVinci Resolve is the best free editor for beginners, introduces a team member who will teach the content, and outlines the tutorial structure—a mix of a Level One basic edit and an Advanced Edit, with a full account of Resolve’s layout and seven-page interface.

sections.title: Importing Media & Project Setup
concepts: drag-and-drop folder import to preserve folder structure
project frame rate prompt and vertical timeline option
sections.description: Shows how to import footage into Resolve via the Media Pool, demonstrates importing as a folder to keep folder structure, and explains project settings like timeline resolution and vertical (1080x1920) format for social content, plus the file-frame rate considerations.

sections.title: Level One Edit: Framing, Cuts & Basic Tools
concepts: keyboard navigation (arrow keys, space, L, J, K)
sections.description: Introduces core editing actions: placing clips on the timeline, basic playback controls, cutting with the blade tool, moving clips with the selection tool, and using the inspector for transform and audio adjustments. Emphasizes efficient navigation with keyboard shortcuts and timeline zoom.

sections.title: Color Grading & Audio Enhancement
concepts: LUTs and LUT import workflow (Sony LUT)
sections.description: Dives into color grading using a LUT (Sony LUT) and manual tweaks via color wheels, including explanations of lift, gamma, gain, and offset. Also covers white balance adjustments and audio workflow, including normalization to a target peak and enabling a compressor in the Fairlight mixer.

sections.title: B-Roll, Transitions, and Intro Text
concepts: transitions (Push with motion blur, ease in/out)
text overlays and DaVinci Resolve logo
sections.description: Demonstrates adding B-roll to support the talking head narrative, applying and tweaking transitions with motion blur and easing, and building attention-grabbing intro text and logo overlays. Emphasizes using transitions strategically rather than on every clip, with examples like push and a pop effect.

sections.title: Advanced Techniques: Masking, Clones & Sound Design
concepts: masking with Pen Tool and Alpha Output
sections.description: Presents advanced compositing: isolating a subject with masking and tracking, replacing the background, and creating clone/ghost effects. Also covers precise timing of sound effects and discusses captioning options, including automatic captions in Studio and manual captioning workflows.
